key_insight: BridgeSRDA generates probabilistic high-resolution flow reconstructions from low-resolution forecasts and sparse observations, approaching high-resolution ensemble-filter accuracy at lower runtime.
engineering_relevance: The framework could reduce the computational cost of ensemble flow-state estimation while supporting retrospective reconstruction and short-range nowcasting.
method: Combine low-resolution numerical forecasts with sparse, noisy observations.
Learn forecast-informed stochastic transport and sample high-resolution analysis ensembles.
Use each current analysis to initialize the next low-resolution forecast.
evidence_signal: Across ten independently initialized 3D quasi-geostrophic trajectories in a narrow-jet regime different from training, BridgeSRDA reduced the mean absolute error ratio by approximately 32.5% versus deterministic 4D-SRDA and took approximately 17 s per 30-member analysis versus 31 s for the high-resolution ensemble filter under recorded conditions.
watch_item: Uncertainty remains undercalibrated: nominal 90% intervals covered approximately 62% of reference values, with boundary spread artifacts and reduced skill under sparser observations.
paper_title: BridgeSRDA: Efficient Probabilistic Super-Resolution Data Assimilation with Forecast-Informed Stochastic Interpolants
